capability_investigated:
The processor(...) feature-extraction step and generate(features, prompts, ...)
batch interface. Studied what the WhisperFeatureExtractor does with raw audio
and what shapes generate accepts for features and prompts.
what_i_learned:
The feature extractor collapses any-length audio into a single 30s window
(3000 mel frames), so the stub silently deletes everything past 0:30 — a pure
deletion failure on multi-minute calls. It also accepts a list of audio arrays
and stacks them into a [N, 128, 3000] batch, and generate already accepts that
batched tensor with a per-window list of prompts, returning N results.
hypothesis:
Split audio into <=30s windows, run them as one batched generate call, and
join the per-window decodes. This recovers the truncated tail (the dominant
deletion axis) with no new import and a single decode pass within budget.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_no_speech_prob decoding kwarg and the per-window
no_speech_prob field on each WhisperGenerationResult — a return value the
current pipeline never requests or reads.
what_i_learned:
The backend's generate() accepts return_no_speech_prob=True and then each
result in the returned list carries a scalar no_speech_prob, giving a
per-window voice-activity signal directly from the model. This lets a
multi-window pipeline distinguish real speech windows from trailing silence
padding without any external VAD, addressing hallucination on the padded
final chunk while full-coverage windowing fixes the dominant deletion.
hypothesis:
Tile the audio into consecutive 30s windows (covers content past 0:30 that
the stub deletes), batch-decode them, and drop windows with
no_speech_prob > 0.85 so silence padding does not emit hallucinated text;
concatenate the surviving window texts.
